title: Popup sizes and Session Files — see them together

steps.path: Support YouCoded; About; Submit a ticket; Assistant settings
steps.headline: Which approach to the four dialog sizes should we explore?
steps.notice: These are representative popups, captured together at the same browser size; widths are ceilings, not minimums.
steps.risk: This chooses a direction to mock, not a new app-wide rule or permission to resize existing popups.

options.label: Keep four roles
pros: Each size matches its job: quick prompt, ordinary panel, document, or two-column window.
cons: Four choices to remember; less obvious which one a new popup needs.
options.summary: Formalize what each size is for, without changing these screens.

options.label: Combine small sizes
pros: One fewer size to choose; short dialogs and ordinary panels line up.
cons: Quick confirmations may grow wider, or some panels may crowd their text.
options.summary: Test prompt and panel at one shared size; leave document and wide alone.

options.label: Fit the content
pros: Short and long content can use the width they actually need.
cons: Dialogs may feel less consistent and could change size as their contents load.
options.summary: Try a bounded, content-led width before selecting named sizes.

steps.path: Project switcher; Tags & note; Resume Session; Marketplace Details
steps.headline: How far should a common popup style extend beyond the four dialogs?
steps.notice: These are different jobs: a search palette, compact editor, two-pane browser, and near-fullscreen details view.
steps.risk: Keeping distinct sizes does not prevent titles, close controls, and scroll edges from using an approved treatment where reviewed.

options.label: Keep distinct roles
pros: Search, editing, browsing, and full details keep their useful layouts.
cons: More shell styles remain to document and check for drift.
options.summary: Formalize each class and review shared details per shell.

options.label: Unify outer chrome
pros: Headers and dismiss controls feel related without squeezing the content.
cons: The four shapes still differ, and some headers need exceptions.
options.summary: Mock common outer headings, close controls and edges across eligible classes.

options.label: Fewer classes
pros: Fewer sizes and layouts to learn and maintain.
cons: A compact note editor may inherit too much space; a two-pane browser may become cramped.
options.summary: Try merging only the compact popup and search palette into dialog roles first.

steps.path: Right-click a message; open a file in Project Files
steps.headline: Should anchored menus and near-fullscreen file views follow the dialog size ladder?
steps.notice: The menu opens beside your click; the file detail needs most of the screen. Neither is a centered, reading-sized dialog.
steps.risk: This decides their relationship to a future popup rule, not their individual styling or behavior.

options.label: Keep them separate
pros: Each keeps its useful placement and size.
cons: The guide must spell out more exceptions.
options.summary: Name anchored menus and large file views as distinct classes.

options.label: Share compatible parts
pros: Common surfaces and dismiss controls can feel related.
cons: There is no useful common width or header for a right-click menu and a file view.
options.summary: Keep placements but test only compatible chrome per class.

steps.path: Open the file list beside a conversation
steps.headline: Which file entry is most useful in Session Files?
steps.notice: Only the file cards change; Project Files keeps its grid and list. The screenshots show file previews from the app's own viewer, using sample files.
steps.risk: Small text previews can crop awkwardly; unsupported or unavailable files show an extension label, and these pictures do not verify Android behavior.

variants.label: Today's rows
variants.summary: Continuous file list. Most entries fit, but boundaries between files are quiet.

variants.label: Cards, no preview
variants.summary: The compact card direction previously picked; no extra file read or potentially misleading thumbnail.

variants.label: Square preview
variants.summary: A 44px left square shows actual supported file content or an extension fallback; text is often cropped.

variants.label: Wide preview
variants.summary: A 72 × 44px left rectangle gives visual files more room, while using more of the filename width.
